tasks.short: Modify the nursing treatment plan when the patient's response changes.

steps.what: Note patients' responses and conditions at the bedside.
Read the active treatment plan on the patient record.
Decide how to modify the treatment plan.
Draft the modified treatment plan from that decision.

loop.input: The bedside response note from s1 and the plan decision from s3. No vital-sign feed and no medicine code.
loop.output: Draft lines of the modified nursing treatment plan.
loop.check: Every sentence states only a change the plan decision already names, and points at a phrase in the bedside response note. It adds no intervention, dose, frequency or medicine.
loop.stop: One pass. If any sentence fails the check, the draft stays blank and the nurse writes the lines.
loop.why_not_simpler: The decision is free text. A fixed template cannot phrase the change, and a rule cannot tell a supported change from a line the note does not state.

steps.what: Check the draft cites the decision and bedside note.
File the confirmed treatment plan on the patient record.
Tell the patient what the treatment plan now says.

tasks.design: The nurse still notes responses, reads the active plan, decides the change, and tells the patient. A draft in {OTHER}, the electronic patient record, phrases only the plan decision from s3 and the bedside note from s1, and stays blank if a line adds an intervention. The nurse confirms that text before {OTHER} stores it. No microphone is used.
tasks.previous_blocker: The reason for a plan change was free text typed after the round, often a second time into the record.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded loop can phrase only a decision and a note the nurse already wrote, and the record can store that text after the nurse confirms it.
tasks.still_hard: The clinical decision, a thin bedside note, and any change to a prescription.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing whether the patient is coping, and refusing a plan line the bedside note does not support.

ambition.what: Confirm or leave the nursing plan the same shift the response is noted, including changes that used to wait for the formal review.

tasks.altitude: The nurse still decides every plan change and still tells the patient. The week loses the second typing of a change already decided. Prescription rights do not move.

reach.learn: Which nursing lines the nurse confirmed, and that a blank draft is not a request to prescribe.

reach.task: Take the next shift from the filed plan
reach.learn: Read the confirmed plan, not the draft.

evidence.claim: Autoscriber records the consultation, the clinician validates, and the note can be stored in the patient record.
Across 236,153 generated notes in one European health system, self-estimated time per note fell from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes.
A prescription comes from a named practitioner.
The patient dossier is kept twenty years after the last change.
Providers must know whether a generative tool is a medical device, assess risks, train, test and monitor it.
Ambient recording that captures staff performance needs works-council consent.

assumptions: This task changes nursing interventions on an existing plan. It does not prescribe, stop a medicine, or allocate staff.

The draft's only inputs are the bedside response note, produced in s1, and the plan decision, produced in s3. Both stay at remaining 100 because the design does not shorten noticing or deciding. The loop does not read a vital-sign feed or a medicine code.

The active treatment plan the nurse reads in s2 is already stored: fields are problem, nursing intervention, frequency, last review time and author. Producer is the registered nurse who last saved it. Fallback is the paper care plan, read in s2. That earlier save is not re-captured here and is not counted as saved.
Filing in s6 stores only the confirmed text from s5. A blank draft means the nurse writes the lines and the filing step does not run.
No ambient microphone. Works-council consultation still applies to edit logs on care notes. The study minutes on generated notes are not this task's saving.

Where the digest names Dutch rules, the dossier retention period and the named-practitioner prescription rule apply. Elsewhere, national rules apply. The one hour per 100 baseline hours is a monthly sample of filed changes for lines the note does not support.
unknowns: Whether this employer's nurses may file a nursing plan change without a physician countersignature.
Whether the works council has already consented to edit logs on care notes.
research_questions: What share of treatment-plan changes on this ward are nursing interventions rather than prescription changes?

already_counted.description: Reading the draft against the bedside note and the plan decision.

incremental.description: Monthly sample of filed plan changes for a line the bedside note does not support.

approvals.approved_version: Modified nursing treatment plan for this patient and shift, as the registered nurse confirmed it against the bedside note. A later change voids the confirmation. This file is not a prescription.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only the second writing of a change already decided is drafted, and only the filing of the confirmed text is configured. Noticing, reading the plan, the decision and telling the patient stay at full time. Thin notes leave the draft blank, so the nurse writes the lines. One hour per 100 baseline hours is the monthly sample. The published note-time study is not applied here.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Visit patients and observe nurses to see that care is proper.

steps.what: Drop the recopied list of patients for this visit.
Visit patients and observe whether the nursing care is proper.
Speak with the nurses about the care just observed.
Write the visit finding on proper nursing care.

tasks.design: The charge nurse still visits patients, speaks with nurses, and writes the finding. The paper copy of the ward list stops because {OTHER}, the electronic patient record, already holds bed, patient identifier and named nurse, produced by the ward clerk at admission and transfer. A late transfer is still read from the whiteboard.
tasks.previous_blocker: The round is watching care in the room. Names were copied onto paper when the whiteboard and the bed record disagreed.
tasks.enabler_now: The bed record already holds those names, so the second copy can stop. No model is required, and nothing scores the nurse.
tasks.still_hard: The visit itself, and a bed record that lags a transfer.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing care that looks correct on a list and is wrong in the room.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in the round. The paper copy of names already on the bed record stops. The nurse still decides what the visit showed.

reach.task: Review nursing care on the ward
reach.learn: Use the visit finding the charge nurse wrote. There is no score of the nurse.

evidence.claim: A ward bed list already stored at admission can replace a second paper copy of the same names. This is model knowledge.
Ambient recording that captures staff performance needs works-council consent.

assumptions: The gone step is only the charge nurse's second copy of names. Visits, conversations and the written finding stay at remaining 100. The design does not shorten noticing or the talk with nurses.

Ward bed list contract: fields are bed, patient identifier and named nurse. Producer is the ward clerk at admission and transfer, in the electronic patient record. That capture stays the clerk's work, is not part of this task's 100, and is not counted as saved. Fallback is the whiteboard. A name missing after a transfer is copied by the nurse, which is the 0.3 hour allowance.
The visit finding is prose the charge nurse writes. No model drafts it and no score of the nurse is stored. No microphone is used.
Upkeep is the 0.3 hour exception copy, not zero.
unknowns: How often this ward's bed record lags the whiteboard after a transfer.
research_questions: On a typical shift, how many names on the paper round list are already on the bed record?

incremental.description: Copy a name from the whiteboard when a transfer is missing from the bed record.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only the recopied ward list goes. The visit, the talk with nurses and the written finding stay at full time. When the bed record lags, the nurse still copies that name, which is the 0.3 hour allowance. Some wards already skip the paper list, so the low end is zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assess home or work environments for health or safety problems.

steps.what: Assess home or work environments for health or safety problems.
Hear individuals and families state their health needs.
Decide the problems found for individuals, families or communities.
Draft the assessment record from the visit notes.

loop.input: The environment note from s1, the stated needs from s2, and the problem decision from s3. No risk score and no referral code.
loop.check: Every problem sentence cites a phrase in the environment note, the stated needs or the problem decision. It adds no problem, score or referral.
loop.stop: One pass. If any sentence fails, the draft stays blank and the nurse writes the assessment.
loop.why_not_simpler: The visit note is free text. A checklist cannot phrase what the nurse saw, and a score would invent a problem the decision did not name.

steps.what: Check the assessment draft against those visit notes.
File the confirmed assessment of health or safety problems.

tasks.design: The home or work visit, the conversation and the decision stay with the nurse. A draft in {OTHER}, the electronic patient record, phrases only the environment note, the stated needs and the problem decision, and stays blank if it adds a problem. The nurse confirms the assessment before {OTHER} files it.
tasks.previous_blocker: The assessment is what the nurse sees on site. The write-up repeated that prose later in the record.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded loop can phrase notes the nurse already wrote, and stop when a sentence adds a problem the decision did not name.
tasks.still_hard: The visit, and any problem the nurse has not yet named.
tasks.human_edge: Judging a home or workplace the record cannot see, including what the family does not say.

ambition.what: Record a health or safety problem the day of the visit, including problems that used to sit in a notebook until the weekly write-up.

tasks.altitude: The nurse still makes the assessment in the home or workplace. Write-up is shorter only when the note already names the problem. No risk score is added.

reach.task: Follow up a home safety problem
reach.learn: Which problems the nurse confirmed from the visit, and which lines were left blank.

evidence.claim: Autoscriber records the consultation, the clinician validates, and the note can be stored in the patient record.
Providers must know whether a generative tool is a medical device, assess risks, train, test and monitor it.
The patient dossier is kept twenty years after the last change.
Solely automated decisions that significantly affect a person need a stated basis.
Medical-device rules are listed among the product laws the AI Act points to.
AI that falls under a listed product law and needs a notified-body assessment is high-risk.

assumptions: Producers counted in this task, all at remaining 100: s1 writes the environment note, s2 records stated needs, s3 names each problem. The draft uses only those three texts. It does not read a risk score, a safety flag or a referral code.
If a customer later wants a structured safety code, the nurse must tick it inside s3 and that tick stays in s3's time. This design does not add that code.
A blank draft means the nurse writes the assessment. Filing stores only the confirmed text and does not suggest a diagnosis.
Dutch dossier retention applies where the digest names it. Elsewhere, national rules apply. The 0.8 hour is a monthly sample of filed assessments for a sentence the visit notes do not support.
unknowns: Whether home-care and hospital assessments use the same patient record at this employer.
Whether a community assessment that names no individual is filed on a patient record or a program file.
research_questions: What share of these assessments are home visits, workplace visits, or community visits with no single patient?

already_counted.description: Reading the assessment draft against the visit notes and the problem decision.

incremental.description: Monthly sample of filed assessments for a sentence the visit notes do not support.

approvals.approved_version: Assessment of health or safety problems from this visit, as the registered nurse confirmed it against the visit notes. A later change voids the confirmation.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The visit, the conversation and the decision stay at full time. The draft only phrases notes the nurse already wrote, and stays blank when a line adds a problem. The 0.8 hour is the monthly sample. High is 10, under the net after that sample.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan and run a health program with individuals, families or groups.

steps.what: Meet individuals, families or groups about the health program.
Decide the program aim for these communities.
Choose the vetted page that matches the program aim.
Draft the program outline from the aim and that page.

loop.input: The program aim from s2 and the page the nurse chose in s3, including its paragraph text. No other source.
loop.check: Every sentence quotes the chosen page or the program aim, and adds no health claim the page does not state.
loop.stop: One pass. If the nurse recorded no page, or any sentence fails, the outline stays blank and the nurse writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: The page is prose. A template cannot pick the paragraph that matches this aim, and a search snippet would not prove the sentence is on the page.

steps.what: Check each outline sentence against the chosen page.
Accept the program outline before the group sees it.
Release the accepted program outline to the group.
Implement the health program in the group session.

tasks.design: Meetings and the group session stay in person. The nurse chooses a page already stored in {DOCS}; the choice is s3 and stays at full time. A draft quotes only that page and the aim, and the nurse manager accepts it before {DOCS} releases the outline.
tasks.previous_blocker: Program text for a public group was written from memory. A draft must not invent a health claim.
tasks.enabler_now: A stored guideline page can be quoted once the nurse has chosen it. The session stays in the room.
tasks.still_hard: The session itself, and an aim that has no vetted page.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing what this group will actually do, and dropping a page that does not fit them.

ambition.what: Refresh the program outline when the aim changes, including aims that previously waited for the annual leaflet.

tasks.altitude: The nurse still chooses the page and still runs the session. A written outline exists before the session only when a vetted page fits. The manager still accepts public text.

reach.learn: Reject an outline sentence that the chosen page does not state.

evidence.claim: Thuisarts publishes guideline-based information for the public, from the professional bodies and the patient federation.
A person must be told when they are interacting with an AI system.
Quoting a page the nurse has already chosen is a reading aid. The nurse still runs the session. This is model knowledge.

assumptions: Vetted page contract: fields are page id, title, paragraph text and approving body. Producer of the library is the guideline owner. A document administrator loads the page into the document store before this task. That load is not this task's time and is not counted as saved. Fallback: s3 records no page and the outline stays blank.
Producer of the page used here is s3, the nurse's choice, at remaining 100. Producer of the aim is s2, also at remaining 100. The draft reads no other source.

The group session in s8 stays at remaining 100. It is the nurse speaking, not a chatbot. If a later channel lets the public talk to the draft, the disclosure duty applies and this design does not open that channel.
The 0.8 hour is upkeep when a stored page is withdrawn and linked outlines must be checked. It is not zero.
unknowns: Whether a guideline page library is already loaded in the document store, and which body approved it.
Whether the nurse manager is the role that may release public health text here.
research_questions: What share of program aims have a matching page already in the document store?

already_counted.description: Reading each outline sentence against the chosen page.
The nurse manager's acceptance of that outline.

incremental.description: Recheck an outline when the stored page it quotes is withdrawn.

approvals.approved_version: Program outline for this aim, quoted from the page the nurse chose, as the nurse manager accepted it. A later change voids the acceptance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Meetings, the page choice, the manager's acceptance and the group session stay at full time. The outline is drafted only from the chosen page and stays blank when no page fits. The 0.8 hour is the check after a withdrawn page. Manager time is outside the nurse's saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The nurse still assesses patients, visits the ward and runs community sessions. The record keeps confirmed wording. Prescription rights and the round itself do not move.
reach: Physician: read a confirmed nursing plan change and still issue any prescription.
Nurse manager: accept a program outline only when each sentence is on the page the nurse chose.
Incoming nurse: take the shift from the confirmed plan, not from a draft.
skills_to_grow: Leave a plan or assessment draft blank when the note does not support the line.
Choose a vetted page and reject a sentence that page does not say.
Write the visit finding in your own words.
role.ambitious_version: One patient record holds the confirmed nursing plan and the confirmed assessment, each line traceable to a note from that visit. A community outline quotes a page the nurse chose and a manager accepted. The nurse still decides, visits and runs the session.
